description:
FILED s473 (Fable, 2026-09-06).  EVIDENCE: Fable gate on BT worktree (main 2e39cc67 + docs-only commits; NO cl/ or Pl/ change): Pl/t/moo-01.t 0/15 -- every row <missing>; the captured sbcl output (archived ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s470/s470bt-agent-a7e4df2d4d7592f04/fable-gate.log around line 640) ends in
  Unhandled sb-int:simple-file-error ... :PATHNAME #P"/home/bernt/.pcl-cache/modules/2FC4CDA40DB008AD.deps" :MESSAGE "No such file or directory" ... (:WRITE-DATE ...)
  7: (PCL::P-CLEANUP-OLD-CACHE)  8: (PCL::P-LOAD-MODULE-CACHED ".../Sub/Quote.pm")
The entry exists again with mtime 17:49 = DURING the gate: a concurrent process (BX or BY, the two agents sharing the cache from other worktrees) replaced it, and the window between `directory` and `file-write-date` was hit.  Re-run alone: 15/15.  So: NOT a BT regression; a pre-existing race in the runtime that any two concurrent PCL processes can hit (two users, two CI jobs, prove -j8 itself).

CAUSE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `p-cleanup-old-cache` (~18442, main 637fc58e):
  (dolist (file (directory ...)) (when (< (file-write-date file) cutoff) (ignore-errors (delete-file file))))
only the DELETE is inside ignore-errors; the `file-write-date` is not, and it signals when the file is gone.  The prune runs on EVERY module-cache miss, inside the load of an unrelated module, so the die kills the program.

FIX SHAPE (rule 12 boundary, s329: this is EFFECT-ONLY hygiene -- a vanished file is simply not ours to prune; never a die): every per-file operation in the prune (stat / write-date / utime / delete) treats ENOENT as SKIP -- e.g. `(let ((d (ignore-errors (file-write-date file)))) (when (and d (< d cutoff)) (ignore-errors (delete-file file))))`.  The SAME rule for the other side of the shared cache: `p-cache-valid-p`s read of `<key>.deps` (a manifest that vanishes or is half-replaced mid-read is a MISS, not a die), `%p-note-cache-use`s utime (BY, #1300 item B), and BYs `%p-prune-dir` / `.last-prune` claim.  s470bw made the WRITE side atomic (temp + rename); this is the READ/PRUNE side.  A guard row: a cache dir with a dangling entry that disappears under the prune cannot be staged deterministically in a test -- stage the EQUIVALENT: a `.deps` whose `.lisp` is missing, and a `.lisp` whose `.deps` is missing, both must be a MISS + a clean load (say which; the ENOENT-inside-the-window branch is by inspection).

OWNER: BY (#1300) if it can absorb it under the s366 filler rule (same mechanism -- BY rewrote the prune as `%p-prune-dir`); otherwise its own filler right after BY merges.  Companion: none (runtime hygiene); a full sweep because cl/ changed.  ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the s473 restart ran three trees on one ~/.pcl-cache (Fable gate + BX + BY) -- the cache is shared by DESIGN (one user, one dir), so a per-worktree isolation is not the fix; the readers must be race-tolerant.
=== DONE (s470by) ===

Absorbed into #1300 under the filler rule (the same mechanism that batch
rewrote), in two rounds.

THE FILED DIE WAS ALREADY GONE.  Items A-D had rewritten the prune as
%p-prune-dir with the stat inside ignore-errors, so the exact
SB-INT:SIMPLE-FILE-ERROR the task was filed on could no longer escape.  That is
why 6 of the 9 first-round guard rows pass on the parent commit too -- said
plainly rather than claimed as a fix.

ROUND 1 -- the REST of the family.  Five more places asked PROBE-FILE and then
FILE-WRITE-DATE (p-cache-valid-p twice, %p-note-cache-use, %p-claim-prune,
%p-fasl-build-refused-p) and one LOAD of a fasl that may have gone since the
check.  ONE READING (rule 11): %P-MTIME is now the runtime's only
(file-write-date) -- grep says exactly one -- and it answers NIL instead of
signalling.  NIL means SKIP on the hygiene side and MISS on the validity side:
the s329 boundary, effect-only, so not rule 12's die.  %P-LOAD-MODULE-FASL gains
a file-error arm narrowed to "the fasl is no longer there", so a file error
raised BY the module's own top-level code still propagates.

ROUND 2 -- THE FILE THE RACE WAS MEASURED ON WAS A WRITER'S IN-FLIGHT TEMP
(<key>-<hex>-<pid>.fasl), so this is not a two-agents problem: prove -j8's own
siblings do it.  The prune now does not ask about temps at all.
%P-CACHE-TEMP-PATH is the ONE construction both writers publish through
(%p-write-cache-file and %p-build-module-fasl each built the name inline -- the
duplication that lets a reader's idea of a temp drift from a writer's) and
%P-CACHE-TEMP-P the one recognition.  The suffix became -tmp<pid> rather than
-<pid>: an entry's name is uppercase hex and a bare -<digits> would collide with
the ~0.5 % of fasl identity fields that are all decimal digits.  THE COST, in the
docstring: a temp whose writer crashed is never pruned -- one small file per
crash; the alternative is deleting a file another process owns.

GUARDS: Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t 37 -> 46 -> 50.  The window itself cannot be
staged from outside the process (an ENOENT arriving BETWEEN two calls needs a
scheduler, not a fixture; a dangling symlink does not do it -- SBCL's
FILE-WRITE-DATE answers the LINK's own date, probed), so the rows assert the
invariant that makes the window harmless -- exactly one mtime read and it is
%p-mtime -- plus the helper's contract asked of the runtime, the two HALF
ENTRIES the race really leaves (a .deps whose .lisp is gone and the reverse:
both a MISS and a clean load), and the temp row (a temp-shaped and an ordinary
file, both 40 days old: the prune leaves the temp and deletes the ordinary one,
the control saying the prune really ran).

ACCEPTANCE: one whole gate with no race signature -- 216 files / 7517 rows, Result FAIL = only the 13 pclxs xs rows and
`grep -a -c write-date` over its log = 0.  Normative in ir-spec 9.2b: the temp
naming rule and "a missing mtime means SKIP or MISS, never an error".
subject: BUG (shared-cache RACE): p-cleanup-old-cache dies when a module-cache entry VANISHES between the directory listing and its stat -- the file-error escapes the prune and KILLS the unrelated program that was loading a module (moo-01.t 0/15 in a gate while two sibling trees wrote the same ~/.pcl-cache)
